record.paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
record.original_question: Can source terms in three-fluid hydrodynamics, where two baryon-rich projectile and target fluids generate a fireball fluid, provide a correct explanation of how baryon deposition occurs in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions?

evidence.quote: Investigate if the source terms in 3-fluid-hydrodynamics [21] with two baryon-rich projectile and target fluids that create the fireball fluid can provide an understanding of the baryon deposition

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies (of order a few to tens of GeV per nucleon), one observes a redistribution of net baryon number from the colliding nuclei into the central rapidity region — the phenomenon of baryon deposition (or baryon stopping). A standard hydrodynamic framework for modeling such collisions is three-fluid hydrodynamics, in which the matter is described by three coupled relativistic fluids:

(i) a "projectile" fluid carrying baryon number from the forward-going nucleus,
(ii) a "target" fluid carrying baryon number from the backward-going nucleus, and
(iii) a baryon-free "fireball" fluid of newly produced matter.

Each fluid satisfies its own conservation equations
   ∂_μ T^{μν}_α = F^ν_α,   ∂_μ N^μ_α = J_α,   α ∈ {p, t, f},
with phenomenological source/friction terms F^ν_α and J_α coupling the fluids and transferring energy, momentum, and baryon charge from the projectile and target fluids into the fireball fluid, subject to global conservation Σ_α F^ν_α = 0 and Σ_α J_α = 0.

Problem. Determine whether source terms of this form, coupling two baryon-rich projectile and target fluids to a fireball fluid in three-fluid hydrodynamics, can give a quantitatively correct description of baryon deposition (the rapidity distribution of net baryon number, including any double-peak structure and central-rapidity stopping) in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies. Identify functional forms of the friction/source terms F^ν_α, J_α, and an associated equation of state, for which the resulting net-baryon rapidity distributions agree with experimental data over the relevant beam-energy range, or else show that no such choice within the three-fluid framework can do so.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2023–2025) continue to develop and refine multi-fluid hydrodynamic descriptions of heavy-ion collisions, including new formulations of friction/source terms and comparisons with baryon-stopping data. While three-fluid hydrodynamics has had partial success reproducing net-baryon rapidity distributions, the question of whether such source terms provide a fully correct, quantitative explanation of baryon deposition at intermediate energies remains an active research topic with no settled answer.

status_evidence.title: Friction terms in the multi-fluid description of heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: The key part of a multi-fluid model is the formulation of the interaction between the fluids, called friction, which defines how the fluids affect each other's hydrodynamic variables.
status_evidence.claim: Friction/source terms in multi-fluid hydrodynamics remain an active modeling problem in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Simulating collectivity in dense baryon matter with multiple fluids
status_evidence.snippet: A three-fluid hydrodynamic model for simulating relativistic heavy-ion collisions includes two baryon-rich fluids along with a third, baryon-free fluid of newly produced particles.
status_evidence.claim: The three-fluid framework with baryon-rich projectile/target and a fireball fluid is still being developed and applied.

status_evidence.title: Baryon stopping and charge deposition in heavy-ion collisions due to gluon saturation
status_evidence.snippet: Baryon stopping and charge deposition in heavy-ion collisions due to gluon saturation.
status_evidence.claim: Baryon deposition mechanisms remain under active investigation through alternative (non-three-fluid) approaches as of 2025.
